parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: A comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1 (separator V-001 and associated lines) was executed systematically across all six source elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures. Rather than being biased by the salient training vignette regarding electrical-induced well shutdown and low flow, the analysis examines the full operational envelope including overpressure, low/high level carryover and blowby, thermal deviations, material degradation, and procedural errors during startup. All findings are strictly grounded in the provided packet facts.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Organizational factor domain: Excluded per SYS-09 which states classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions and forbids inventing organizational facts.
Electrical system well shutdown: Excluded from primary Node 1 findings as it originated from a fictional external training vignette providing no plant-specific evidence.
Reverse flow from fuel gas header / burn pit: Unresolved due to lack of backpressure and check valve data in the packet.
External Fire/Explosion: Excluded as non-applicable within Node 1 internal process deviations without external fire protection/deluge data.

consequences: Vessel overpressurization beyond nominal 60 psig toward or exceeding published operating condition boundary of 125 psig
Potential loss of primary containment or structural failure of V-001

evidence.relevance: Defines Node 1 as V-001 separator and associated lines
Establishes nominal 60 psig and published operating condition text of 125 psig
Documents gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies PIT-101, PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Downstream blockage in the separated gas line to the fuel gas header or burn pit
Inlet gas surge exceeding gas venting capacity
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B sizing and setpoints against upper operating limits (125 psig) and design specifications
Confirm fail-open action of PV-101 upon loss of signal or instrument air

consequences: Liquid carryover into the gas outlet line
Hydrocarbon or water entering the fuel gas system or burn pit, creating burner issues or flare liquid carryover hazards

evidence.relevance: V-001 is a three-phase separator for gas, oil, and free water
Details oil routing to Heater-Treater and water to water treatment
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Discharge line restriction to Heater-Treater or water treatment
Liquid inflow surge exceeding liquid removal rate
recommendations: Verify high-high level alarm and interlock logic to close inlet SDV-30010 on high liquid level in V-001
Ensure independent level alarms for both oil and water compartments

consequences: Loss of liquid seal in V-001 leading to gas blowby into downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment systems
Potential overpressurization of lower-pressure downstream equipment

evidence.relevance: Details downstream connection to Heater-Treater separator and V-003 Desalter
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: Prolonged drain with reduced liquid feed
recommendations: Verify low-low level trip logic on SDV-101 and SDV-102 to isolate outlets on loss of liquid level
Confirm downstream piping and vessel pressure ratings against gas blowby pressure

consequences: Process starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Disruption of separation equilibrium and potential loss of liquid levels in V-001

evidence.relevance: Specifies downstream process sequence V-001 to Heater-Treater to Desalter

possible_causes: Upstream well shut-in or pipeline restriction
recommendations: Confirm FAL-103 alarm annunciation and operational procedures for orderly downstream unit standby during prolonged low-flow conditions

consequences: Operating temperature deviating outside nominal 130 °F or published upper condition of 200 °F
Impaired phase separation efficiency and emulsion breaking in V-001 and downstream Heater-Treater

evidence.relevance: Specifies nominal temperature 130 °F and operating condition text up to 200 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger in Node 1

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger design controls
possible_causes: Malfunction, tube fouling, or utility upset in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Significant temperature variations in raw inlet crude
recommendations: Install temperature monitoring and alarms on E-001 process outlet to ensure feed to V-001 remains within design operating limits (130 °F to 200 °F)

consequences: Wall thinning or localized pitting in V-001 lower shell, water boot, and water drain line
Loss of primary containment leading to hydrocarbon and produced water release

evidence.relevance: Free Water Knock-Out separator continuously separates free water from oil and gas
Specifies separated water is routed to water treatment

existing_safeguards: Continuous free water separation and routing via LV-102 to water treatment
possible_causes: Prolonged contact with corrosive free water and dissolved salts or acid gases
Erosion from entrained solids in crude feed
recommendations: Establish routine non-destructive wall-thickness inspection and corrosion monitoring on V-001 bottom and water drainage lines

consequences: Hydraulic surge, localized pressure spike, or process upset upon initial feed introduction into V-001

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as a required source-study element
Explicitly defines FWKO start-up without bypass opening as the source-supported procedural item

existing_safeguards: Standard operating procedures (unstated completeness in packet)
possible_causes: Operator omission or procedural error executing FWKO start-up without opening the designated bypass valve
recommendations: Revise FWKO start-up operating procedure to incorporate an explicit check and hold step ensuring the bypass valve is open prior to feed admission
Conduct operator refresher training on FWKO start-up sequence verification

uncertainty_notes: Specific setpoints for PSV-101 A/B and alarm thresholds for FAL-103 and PIT-101 are not detailed in the packet.
Check valve presence and fail-safe positions (fail-open/fail-closed) of control valves are not explicitly stated.
Organizational structures, staffing, and management systems are omitted from the case packet per SYS-09.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWFLOW-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. An electrical-system failure partially shut down the wells and reduced separator flow; generators stopped and the plant entered shutdown. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
